tool_input.description: Rewrite test to use CSRF-primed agent

result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 7 pass / 0 fail. `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures (the 3 warnings are pre-existing missing-test warnings for other controllers).

`ProfileController.update` was reading the raw request body with `this.request.json<ProfileInput>()` — no validation at all — and then spreading that untrusted object straight into `User.forceUpdate()`, which bypasses the fillable allowlist entirely; that combination is what let `not-an-email`, an empty name, and arbitrary extra columns like `id`/`passwordHash` through. The project already had a correct `ProfileUpdateSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts` (trimmed required name capped at 120, trimmed-and-lowercased well-formed email, optional password with an 8-character minimum where empty means "keep the current one") — it just wasn't wired up. I changed `app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts` to run `await this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)`, which yields a 422 with the per-field `errors` shape the profile form already renders and aborts before any write, and to persist through `User.update()` instead of `forceUpdate()`; Zod strips unknown keys so only `name`/`email`/`password` reach the model, and the fillable allowlist is now a second line of defense. Password is still only included when non-empty, so `AuthenticatableModel` re-hashes it only on a real change. I also added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts` covering the three rejection cases, the extra-field-stripping case (asserting `id` and `passwordHash` survive untouched), and the valid-update happy path; it uses a CSRF-primed `actingAs` agent since `PUT /profile` sits behind the app's CSRF middleware.
